c.tagline: Central Java's soulful royal city of palaces, batik, and Javanese tradition.

taxi.fareNote: Blue Bird operates metered taxis; insist on the meter, or use Gojek/Grab for fixed up-front car and motorbike pricing. Traditional becak cycle-rickshaws are negotiated before the ride.

emergency.note: 112 is the general nationwide emergency line; 110 reaches police and 113 the fire service.

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in Pasar Klewer and Pasar Gede market crowds; otherwise usual city awareness.

hood_desc: The historic royal core around the Kraton Surakarta Hadiningrat palace, the Great Mosque and the Kauman batik quarter; the cultural heart, best for sightseeing and tradition on foot.
A centuries-old batik-making village of walled merchant mansions and workshops where you can watch and buy hand-drawn batik; best for batik shopping and heritage lanes.
The main boulevard of Jalan Slamet Riyadi, the city's central artery lined with malls, cafes, hotels and the Sunday car-free market; a convenient, well-connected base in the middle of everything.
A quieter eastern district around Sebelas Maret University (UNS) and the leafy Balekambang park; residential and local, good for a calmer, cheaper stay.
The area around the Pura Mangkunegaran palace and the Ngarsopuro/Pasar Triwindu antique market and night market; best for a mix of royal sights and browsing for crafts and antiques.
lodging: The Royal Surakarta Heritage Solo - MGallery

water.note: Drink bottled or boiled water only.

transit.hours: Batik Solo Trans corridor buses and feeder minibuses run roughly 5:30 AM to 8:00 PM; becak (cycle-rickshaws) and Gojek/Grab cover shorter and later trips.
transit.note: Solo is compact and flat: the Batik Solo Trans (BST) bus rapid transit runs several corridors across the city, supplemented by traditional becak cycle-rickshaws, angkot, the KA Commuter Solo-Yogyakarta line from Solo Balapan, and Gojek/Grab.
transit.pay: BST fares are paid in cash or by e-money card on board (about Rp 3,700, cheaper for students, Rp 7,000 to/from the airport); becak fares are negotiated before the ride; ride-hailing apps use in-app payment or QRIS.

bus: Intercity buses from Tirtonadi Terminal to Yogyakarta, Semarang, Surabaya and across Java

car.idp: Recommended (International Driving Permit required alongside home license)

train: Solo Balapan & Solo Jebres intercity trains to Jakarta, Surabaya and across Java

transit.m: Batik Solo Trans / airport bus to the city (~40 min, ~Rp 7,000)
Adisumarmo Airport Rail Link to Solo Balapan station (~15 min)
Airport taxi to central Solo (25-35 min)

tip.r: Not obligatory; a service charge is often included at larger restaurants and hotels, and rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated but not expected.

food.name: Nasi liwet
food.desc: Rice cooked in coconut milk and chicken stock, topped with shredded chicken, chayote in santan, savoury egg custard and a scoop of thick kumut coconut cream.

places.name: Nasi Liwet Wongso Lemu
places.note: Serving since 1950 on Jalan Teuku Umar; the benchmark nasi liwet, open into the night.

places.name: Keprabon evening liwet stalls
places.note: A row of mat-seated warungs on the same street, all doing the dish from dusk onward.

places.name: Nasi Liwet Bu Sarmi
places.note: Morning version sold in banana-leaf cones to workers and market traders.

food.name: Timlo Solo
food.desc: A clear, sweet-savoury broth poured over sliced sosis Solo egg rolls, chicken liver and gizzard and half a soy-braised egg; light, and eaten at breakfast.

places.name: Timlo Sastro
places.note: Open since 1952 and the name most associated with timlo; a second branch on Jalan Dr Wahidin.

places.name: Timlo Solo Maestro
places.note: Larger, more comfortable room doing the same classic bowl for visitors.

places.name: Pasar Gede food stalls
places.note: Market stalls serve timlo and soto from early morning at the lowest prices in town.

food.name: Tengkleng
food.desc: Goat bones, offal and scraps in a thin, spice-heavy broth, born from what palace kitchens left the servants; eaten with your hands off banana leaf.

places.name: Tengkleng Bu Edi
places.note: Operating since 1971 at the Klewer market gate; sells out fast in the afternoon.

places.name: Tengkleng Rica Pak Manto
places.note: Modern favourite doing both the soupy tengkleng and a fiery rica version.

places.name: Sate Kambing Mbok Galak
places.note: Long-running goat specialist serving tengkleng, tongseng and satay.

food.name: Serabi Notosuman
food.desc: Rice-flour pancakes cooked one at a time in clay pans over charcoal, crisp at the edge and custardy in the middle; plain or chocolate, rolled in banana leaf.

places.name: Serabi Notosuman Ny Lidia
places.note: Part of the family business running since 1923; pans start at 7am and the queue follows.

places.name: Serabi Notosuman Ny Handayani
places.note: The other branch of the original family, a few doors along the same street.

places.name: Pasar Gede stalls
places.note: Market vendors sell serabi and other Javanese jajanan pasar through the morning.

food.name: Selat Solo
food.desc: Java's answer to Dutch biefstuk: thin braised beef with boiled potato, green beans, lettuce and pickles in a sweet, faintly sour soy-and-nutmeg gravy.

places.name: Selat Mbak Lies
places.note: Famous ceramic-cluttered courtyard warung; the classic introduction to selat Solo.

places.name: Selat Viens
places.note: Long-established rival, tidier setting, same colonial-Javanese plate.

places.name: Warung Selat Tenda Biru
places.note: Everyday local version at market prices rather than tourist ones.

food.name: Sate buntel and gudeg ceker
food.desc: Minced goat wrapped in caul fat and grilled into fat sausages, and jackfruit gudeg served with soft-stewed chicken feet - Solo's great late-night pair.

places.name: Sate Kambing Mbok Galak
places.note: One of the city's best-known goat grills; sate buntel is the dish to order.

places.name: Sate Buntel Pak Haji Bejo
places.note: Institution for buntel and tongseng, usually finished by early afternoon.

places.name: Gudeg Ceker Bu Kasno
places.note: Opens around 1am and runs till dawn; the classic Solo after-midnight meal.

food.name: Wedang jahe and wedang ronde
food.desc: Ginger boiled with palm sugar and lemongrass, sometimes with glutinous rice balls of peanut paste floating in it; drunk hot at street wedangan carts after dark.

places.name: Wedangan Pendopo
places.note: Wedangan set in an old Javanese pavilion; ginger drinks with skewers and rice parcels.

places.name: Wedang Ronde Alun-Alun Kidul
places.note: Carts on the palace square selling ronde and jahe to people out late.

places.name: Hik and wedangan carts on Jalan Slamet Riyadi
places.note: Solo's hik carts serve ginger drinks with nasi kucing from evening until small hours.

food.name: Teh nasgitel and es dawet telasih
food.desc: Solo drinks tea panas, legi and kental - hot, sweet and strong. The cold counterpart is dawet with basil seed, jackfruit and coconut milk.

places.name: Es Dawet Telasih Bu Dermi
places.note: Inside the market and famous city-wide; queues form by mid-morning.

places.name: Wedangan Pendopo
places.note: Serves the strong sweet Solo tea alongside the ginger drinks all evening.

places.name: Pasar Gede tea stalls
places.note: Loose Javanese tea sold by the packet and brewed nasgitel-style at the stalls.

landmarks: Keraton Surakarta Hadiningrat (Kasunanan Palace)
The 1745 royal palace of Solo's Susuhunan, a blue-and-white complex of pavilions, sacred heirlooms and a distinctive octagonal Panggung Sangga Buwana tower.
Pura Mangkunegaran
An elegant princely court founded in 1757, where a vast joglo pavilion shelters gamelan orchestras and refined Javanese dance rehearsals visitors may watch.
House of Danar Hadi (Batik Museum)
One of the world's finest batik museums, displaying over a thousand exquisite textiles inside a Dutch-era mansion with a working batik workshop.
Pasar Gede Hardjonagoro
Solo's grand 1930 central market by architect Thomas Karsten, a bustling multi-level hall of tropical produce, jamu herbs and Javanese snacks.
Pasar Klewer
Indonesia's most famous textile market, a labyrinth of hundreds of stalls piled high with batik cloth beside the Kasunanan Palace gates.
Kampung Batik Laweyan
A centuries-old batik-makers' quarter of narrow lanes and merchant mansions, where family workshops still hand-draw wax patterns behind high pastel walls.
Pasar Triwindu
Solo's beloved antiques market, a treasure trove of colonial lamps, wayang puppets, vintage radios and bric-a-brac near Mangkunegaran Palace.
Museum Radya Pustaka
Indonesia's oldest museum, founded in 1890, housing keris daggers, wayang puppets, royal manuscripts and Javanese cultural treasures in a colonial villa.
De Tjolomadoe
A colossal 1861 sugar mill reborn as a cultural hub, its gleaming original machinery forming a dramatic backdrop for concerts and cafés.
Taman Sriwedari
A former royal pleasure garden turned public park, home to tame deer, a lake with rental boats, and a wayang orang theater staging nightly dance-drama.

train.note: No international trains. Solo Balapan is a major junction on Java's southern main line, with frequent trains to Yogyakarta in about an hour, Jakarta in 7-8 hours and Surabaya in 4. The Batara Kresna railbus runs a short scenic line to Wonogiri. Book on the KAI Access app from 45 days out; the Yogyakarta shuttle is very frequent and cheap.

bus.note: No international coaches. Terminal Tirtonadi north of the centre is one of Java's busiest, with Rosalia Indah, Sumber Kencono and others running to Yogyakarta, Semarang, Surabaya and overnight to Jakarta and Bali. Book through redBus Indonesia (https://www.redbus.id/). The Batik Solo Trans city buses connect the terminal, the station and the kraton.

ferry.note: Surakarta is inland in central Java on the Bengawan Solo river, which is not navigable for passengers, so there are no ferries. The nearest ports are Semarang on the north coast, about three hours away.

half.name: Sangiran Early Man Site
half.blurb: UNESCO-listed 'Java Man' fossil museum ~17 km north, one of the world's key hominid excavation sites.

half.name: Tawangmangu (Mt Lawu)
half.blurb: Cool mountain resort on Mt Lawu's slopes with the Grojogan Sewu waterfall and strawberry farms, ~1 hr east.

half.name: Candi Sukuh & Cetho
half.blurb: Mysterious terraced Hindu-Javanese temples on Lawu's flanks with Mesoamerican-looking pyramid forms.

full.name: Yogyakarta
full.blurb: Java's cultural capital ~1 hr by train, gateway to the Borobudur and Prambanan temples.
